The Kuomintang Action Against Mr. Sokolsky and
the North-China Daily News

THE STANDING committee of the Central
Executive Committee of the Kuomintang
Party, the highest organ in the Chinese Na-
tional Government, on April 18, adopted resolutions
which were sent to the State Council for execution,
ordering the suspension of mail privileges to the
North-China Daily News, the official British
newspaper in Shanghai and at the same time
ordering the deportation from China of Mr. George
E. Sokolsky, a member of the staff of that paper.
The meeting at which this action was taken was
presided over by Mr. Sun Fo, Minister of Railways
and a member of the Kuomin Central Executive
Committee. The resolutions were introduced by Mr.
Yeh Chu-tang, chief of the Publicity Division of the
Central Headquarters of the Kuomintang Party.
A detailed report of the meeting of the standing
committee of the Central Executive Committee of the
Kuomintang when the action was taken, which
appeared in the daily reports of the Kuo Wen
(independent) news agency, stated that Mr. Yeh
Chu-tang, declared when the resolutions were
introduced, that the North-China Daily News "had
made ridiculous statement in its columns, creating
baseless sensation. . . detrimental to the interests of
the Chinese nation and causing unwarranted
consternation among foreigners and Chinese." He
also stated that the Ministry of Foreign Affairs had
repeatedly protested against "such nonsense" and had
demanded action through the British Consulate-Gener-
al, but that nothing had resulted from the negotia-
tions. As a result it was decided to ask the Central
Executive. Committee of the Kuomintang to take
official action and issue orders that the Chinese
Maritime Customs and the Chinese Postoffice detain
the copies of the paper and refuse it transmission
through the mail. . Secondly, the Ministry of Foreign
Affairs was instructed to immediately approach the
American Minister in Peiping and the American
Consul-General at Shanghai, and demand the
expulsion of Mr. George E. Sokolsky from China,
Mr. Sokolsky being designated as an American
citizen and a member of the editorial staff of the
North-China Daily News.

The Nanking correspondent of Reuters service,
on April 20, issued the following semi-official
explanation of the Government's action:

"The decision was the result of constant agitation on
the part of the Chinese Press and the proposal of a
number of delegates at the Third National Kuomintang

Congress for some sort of control of the foreign Press in
China. Each time the question of the necessity of the
Government's taking any disciplinary action towards the
so-called anti-Chinese foreign Press is discussed, vigorous
demands are made that such action be taken in regard to
the North China Daily News, which newspaper is
regarded as having 'repeatedly and maliciously attacked
the National Government and the Kuomintang'.

"In recent editorials, the Chin Pao, a semi-official
organ of the Government, said that the North-China Daily
News was an institution which typified the so-called
foreign die-hardism and imperialism, which spread
rumours hoping to create dissension among the Kuomin-
tang ranks and to discredit China and its people in the eyes
of the world. The publication of the reported outbreak
of hostilities some months ago between the Kuomintang
and the former Hankow troops at Wushenkwau, and the
alleged appointment of most of the delegates at the Third
National Kuomintang Congress, were among the numerous
charges made against the newspaper. It may be recalled
that for the reprint of the former story in the Tientsin
Yih Shin Pao, severe disciplinary action was taken by the
Central Kuomintang against that Chinese paper.

"In a reception to the Chinese newspapermen some
time ago, a spokesman of the Central Kuomintang made
a brief review of the foreign Press in China, and in the
course of his address expressed the Party's dissatisfaction
of the alleged anti-Kuomintang tone of the North China
Daily News. Vigorous denunciation was made against
some of the articles written by Mr. George Sokolsky in
that paper on political issues in China. The first official
action was taken, however, when a proposal was submitted
before the Third National Kuomintang Congress asking
for the rigorous suppression of reactionary propaganda.
The proposal stated:

"While the Government is keeping a strict censorship
over Chinese publications, it has paid comparatively little
attention to the foreign Press. A number of the foreign
newspapers and magazines in China are maliciously
attacking our Government and the Party. They are the
mouthpiece of the imperialists. Severe disciplinary action
should be taken against such reactionary publications to
uphold the prestige of the Central Government and the
Party.'

"The proposal bore the signatures of many important
leaders of the Government and the Party, including Mr.
Yeh Chu-tsang, Chairman of the Publicity Department of
the Central Kuomintang, who is also a member of the
Standing Committee of the Central Executive Committee.
The resolution that the North China Daily News be
disciplined and its correspondent, Mr. Sokolsky be
deported, was introduced before the Central Execu-
tive Committee by the Publicity Department of the Central
Kuomintang.

"While the Central Kuomintang will take strong steps
against those foreign publications which are unfriendly

国民党对索科尔斯基先生及《字林西报》采取的行动

中国国民政府最高机关——中国国民党第二届中央执行委员会常务委员会，于4月18日通过决议，并送交行政院执行，命令停止给予上海英方官方报纸《字林西报》（North-China Daily News）邮递特权，同时命令将该报职员乔治·E·索科尔斯基（George E. Sokolsky）先生驱逐出中国。此次采取行动之会议由铁道部部长、国民党中央执行委员会委员孙科先生主持。决议由国民党中央党部宣传部部长叶楚伧先生提出。

据国闻通讯社（独立）每日报道中关于国民党中央执行委员会常务委员会采取该行动时的会议详细报告称，叶楚伧先生在提出决议时宣称，《字林西报》“在其版面上发表荒谬言论，制造无端轰动……损害中华民族利益，并在外侨与华人中引起不必要的恐慌。”他还表示，外交部曾多次就“此类胡言乱语”提出抗议，并通过英国驻沪总领事馆要求采取行动，但谈判未获任何结果。因此，决定请求国民党中央执行委员会采取正式行动，发布命令，由中国海关和中国邮政扣留该报副本，并拒绝通过邮件寄送。其次，指令外交部立即接触驻北平美国公使及驻上海美国总领事，要求将乔治·E·索科尔斯基先生驱逐出中国，索科尔斯基被指称为美国公民及《字林西报》编辑部成员。

路透社南京分社记者于4月20日发布了以下关于政府行动的半官方解释：

“此项决定是中国新闻界不断鼓动，以及第三次全国国民党代表大会上多名代表提议对中国境内的外国报刊进行某种管控的结果。每当讨论政府是否有必要对所谓反华的外国报刊采取纪律行动时，人们都强烈要求针对《字林西报》采取此类行动，该报被视为‘屡次恶意攻击国民政府及国民党’。

“近期，作为政府半官方喉舌的《京报》在社论中指出，《字林西报》是所谓外国顽固主义和帝国主义的典型机构，散布谣言，企图在国民党内部制造分裂，并在世界面前诋毁中国及其人民。该报受到的众多指控中，包括数月前提及国民党与前汉口部队在武胜关发生敌对行动的报道，以及所谓第三次全国国民党代表大会大多数代表的任命事宜。值得回顾的是，此前天津《益世报》因转载前一篇故事，曾遭到国民党中央对该中文报纸的严厉纪律处分。

“不久前在一次接见中国新闻记者的活动中，国民党中央发言人简要回顾了在華外国报刊情况，并在讲话中表达了本党对《字林西报》所谓反国民党基调的不满。会上对该报乔治·索科尔斯基先生撰写的有关中国政治问题的部分文章进行了猛烈抨击。然而，直到第三次全国国民党代表大会提交了一份要求严厉镇压反动宣传的提案后，才采取了首次官方行动。该提案称：

“‘当政府对中文出版物实行严格审查之时，却对外国报刊关注较少。中国境内的若干外国报纸和杂志正在恶意攻击我国政府和本党。它们是帝国主义的喉舌。应对此类反动出版物采取严厉的纪律行动，以维护中央政府和本党的威望。’

“该提案上有许多政府和党内重要领导人的签名，包括国民党中央宣传部部长、同时也是中央执行委员会常务委员会委员的叶楚伧先生。由国民党中央宣传部向中央执行委员会提出了惩处《字林西报》并将其通讯员索科尔斯基先生驱逐出境的决议。

In addition to the foregoing reports the Chinese newspapers have also published considerable regarding the action of the Kuomintang. The Chen Pao, the official Kuomintang Party organ in Nanking on April 19, published an editorial giving details regarding the action against Mr. Sokolsky, the allegation being that he had published articles and circulated propaganda in defense of the Japanese and recently had attacked the Third National Congress of the Kuomintang. There were also other allegations which will be referred to later on in this article. In its issue of Tuesday, April 23, the Sin Wan Pao, one of the leading Chinese newspapers of Shanghai stated that Mr. Wunsz King, Chinese Commissioner of Foreign Affairs, had made an official complaint to the local Consular Body and to the British Consulate-General, asking them to prevent the North-China Daily News from publishing "false statements" or criticism unfavorable to the National Government. The charge was that the official British newspaper here "often published false statements and unfavorable criticism, evidently with the aim of undermining the confidence and respect of the general public in the National Government". Mr. King's letter cited certain articles which had appeared in the paper, one of which was on April 7 stating that "foreigners had received orders to evacuate Nanking" which, according to Mr. King, "was obviously based on erroneous information." It was also stated that the paper had published an editorial on March 29 entitled "The Pity of It" which had disparaged the manifesto issued by the Third Kuomintang Congress and "contained statements which were insulting to the Party and to China." The Commissioner's letter further charged the North-China Daily News with being a "purveyor of rumor....causing an impairment of the friendship and goodwill existing between Great Britain and China." The communication concluded with an expression of hope "that the British Consular authorities will take proper steps in the matter and forward a reply to the Commissioner in regard to his protest."

While the action against the North-China Daily News was precipitated by recent articles and editorials in that paper, some of which were contributed by Mr. Sokolsky, the Chinese resentment is much more deep-seated, this same newspaper having once before been denied the use of the mails by the National Government. As stated in the semi-official explanation of the action which was circulated by Reuters, the paper has generally been looked upon as the organ of "dic-hardism" and reaction, owing to its constant fault-finding and criticism of conditions under the National Government and its general attitude of superiority in respect to things Chinese. Prior to the occupation of Shanghai and the Yangtsze Valley by the Nationalist forces, the North-China Daily News constantly published news reports and editorials alleging the impregnability of the Northern militarists previously in control of this area. Its attacks and reports regarding the alleged excesses of the Nationalist forces were largely responsible for the panicky conditions that prevailed in Shanghai when the Southerners finally occupied this region and this hysteria was in turn transmitted abroad and caused a similar feeling of uneasiness in foreign countries that was responsible for the intervention propaganda and in particular was largely responsible for the action of the British Government in dispatching a military force here that probably was twice as large as the situation demanded for the protection of British lives and properties. If

the truth is ever told regarding the real inspiration for the murderous attacks on foreigners in Nanking by the Chinese military forces that occupied that city, it probably will be found that it constituted Chinese resentment at what they believed was to be the wholesale intervention program of the Powers along lines that had been frequently and openly discussed in the pages of the N. C. D. N., otherwise the occupation of the Yangtsze Valley and the creation of a neutral zone fifty miles wide on each side of that important river to be patrolled by the military forces of the Powers. This constitutes the actual reasons for the Chinese action against the official British newspaper here and hence should not be interpreted as an attack upon the freedom of the press. There is a world of difference between freedom of the press and license. No sovereign country would put up for a minute with the constant attacks and pin-pricking attitude of a foreign newspaper such as has characterized the attitude of the official British organ here. One can easily imagine what would happen if the Paris editions of the New York Herald or Chicago Tribune should adopt a similar critical attitude toward the French Government. It would lead to immediate suppression of the papers and deportation of the editors. And a similar thing would happen if the Japan Advertiser, the American newspaper in Tokyo, should adopt an attitude in respect to the Japanese Government, such as the North-China Daily News constantly adopts toward the Chinese Government and Chinese affairs generally. Newspapers as well as newspapermen are at least expected to act the part of gentlemen when on foreign soil! Need one do more than refer to the statement of Mr. Lloyd George, the Liberal British leader two years ago when he expressed the wish that the British press in China might be printed in the Russian language so that the Russians rather than the British would receive the credit for the mean things that the British newspapers were saying about Chinese nationalism.

Turning to the Kuomintang demand for the deportation of Mr. George E. Sokolsky, the situation is even more pathetic. Mr. Sokolsky, who according to his biographical sketch which appears in the China Who's Who, was born in Utica, N. Y. in 1893, came to China in 1918 from Russia where he had gone from New York City prior to the Kerensky revolution. He was employed for a time on the North China Star, but shortly left that position and came to Shanghai where he was employed on a Kuomintang organ, the Shanghai Gazette. He soon resigned, however, and formed a partnership with a Cantonese named Fred C. Tong and together they were responsible for the organization of what were popularly known as the Shanghai street unions, bodies composed of small shop-keepers and clerks which were largely responsible for the anti-Japanese boycott which spread over China following the decision of the Versailles Conference in awarding the former German interests in Shantung to Japan. Out of the street-union movement grew an organization known as the Chinese Bureau of Public Information, a propaganda which was managed by Tong and Sokolsky and financed by Chinese interests largely for the purpose of spreading anti-Japanese propaganda over the world. It was alleged at the time that there was also a Russian inspiration in the background, but this probably was without foundation. However, Mr. Tong shortly became involved with the Chinese authorities over his alleged connection with the fraudulent promotion of a stock-exchange and finally landed in jail. 除上述报告外，中文报纸也刊登了大量关于国民党行动的报道。4月19日，国民党在南京的官方机关报《晨报》发表社论，详细报道了针对索科尔斯基先生（Mr. Sokolsky）的行动，指控他发表文章并散布宣传以维护日本利益，且最近攻击了国民党第三次全国代表大会。还有其他一些指控，将在本文后文提及。在4月23日（星期二）出版的上海主要中文报纸之一《新闻报》中指出，中国外交专员金问渠先生（Mr. Wunsz King）已向当地领事团及英国总领事馆提出正式抗议，要求他们阻止《字林西报》发布“虚假陈述”或对国民政府不利的批评。指控称，这家在沪的英国官方报纸“经常发布虚假陈述和不利批评，显然旨在破坏公众对国民政府的信任和尊重”。金先生的信函引用了该报刊登的某些文章，其中一篇发表于4月7日，称“外国人已接到撤离南京的命令”，据金先生称，这“显然基于错误信息”。信中还指出，该报于3月29日发表了一篇题为《可怜哉》（The Pity of It）的社论，贬低了国民党第三次全国代表大会发布的宣言，并“包含侮辱党和中国的言论”。这位专员的信函进一步指控《字林西报》是“谣言的传播者……损害了英中之间存在的友谊和善意”。来函最后表示希望“英国领事当局在此事上采取适当措施，并就其抗议向专员作出回复”。

虽然针对《字林西报》的行动是由该报近期的文章和社论引发的（其中部分由索科尔斯基先生撰写），但中国人的不满情绪更为根深蒂固，因为该报此前曾被国民政府禁止使用邮政服务。正如路透社发布的半官方解释所述，由于该报不断挑剔和批评国民政府治下的状况，且在对待中国事物时普遍表现出优越感，因此通常被视为“顽固派”和反动势力的喉舌。在国民革命军占领上海和长江流域之前，《字林西报》不断发布新闻报道和社论，声称此前控制该地区的北方军阀坚不可摧。其对国民革命军所谓暴行的攻击和报道，在很大程度上导致了南方军队最终占领该地区时上海流行的恐慌局面，而这种歇斯底里的情绪又传至国外，引起外国类似的不安情绪，进而导致了干涉主义宣传，特别是很大程度上促使英国政府派遣了一支军事力量来华，其规模可能达到保护英国生命财产所需的两倍之多。如果

关于占领南京的中国军队对外国人进行血腥袭击的真正动机真相大白，人们可能会发现，这构成了中国人对他们认为列强将实施全面干涉计划的愤慨，而这一计划在《字林西报》的版面上已被频繁且公开地讨论过；否则，就是占领长江流域并在该重要河流两侧各建立五十英里宽的由列强军队巡逻的中立区。这构成了中国人针对在沪英国官方报纸采取行动的实际原因，因此不应将其解读为对新闻自由的攻击。新闻自由与肆意妄为之间有着天壤之别。任何一个主权国家都不会容忍一家外国报纸像这家英国官方喉舌那样持续进行攻击和吹毛求疵的态度。人们不难想象，如果《纽约先驱报》或《芝加哥论坛报》的巴黎版对法国政府采取类似的批评态度，会发生什么情况。这将导致报纸立即被查封，编辑被驱逐出境。同样，如果东京的美资报纸《日本广告报》（Japan Advertiser）对日本政府采取《字林西报》对中国政府及一般中国事务常持的态度，也会发生类似的情况。报纸以及报人在异国土地上至少应表现得像个绅士！只需提及两年前英国自由党领袖劳合·乔治先生（Mr. Lloyd George）的声明即可，他表示希望在华的英国报刊能用俄语印刷，这样因英国报纸对中国民族主义所说的刻薄话而获得的“赞誉”将归于俄国人而非英国人。

转而来看国民党要求驱逐乔治·E·索科尔斯基先生（Mr. George E. Sokolsky）一事，情况甚至更为可悲。根据《中国名人录》中刊登的个人简介，索科尔斯基先生1893年出生于纽约州尤蒂卡市，1918年从俄罗斯来到中国，而在克伦斯基革命之前，他从纽约市前往俄罗斯。他曾在《华北明星报》（North China Star）工作了一段时间，但不久便离职来到上海，受雇于国民党机关报《上海公报》（Shanghai Gazette）。然而他很快辞职，并与一位名叫弗雷德·C·唐（Fred C. Tong）的广东人合伙，共同负责组织俗称的上海马路商界联合会，这些团体由小商贩和职员组成，在凡尔赛会议决定将前德国在山东的权益转让给日本后，它们对席卷中国的抵制日货运动负有主要责任。从马路商界联合会运动中衍生出一个名为“中华民国民众情报局”（Chinese Bureau of Public Information）的组织，这是一个由唐和索科尔斯基管理、主要由中方利益集团资助的宣传机构，其目的主要是向世界传播反日宣传。当时有人指控背后还有俄罗斯的动机，但这可能毫无根据。然而，唐先生不久后因涉嫌参与欺诈性推广证券交易所而与中方当局发生纠葛，最终入狱。他们当时出版的一份名为《上海日报》（Shanghai Journal of Com-

Mr. Sokolsky then became manager of the Chinese Government Bureau of Economic Information, which was financed by the old Peiping Government, but from which he finally resigned to become editor of the Far Eastern Review, a monthly engineering journal which has for several years been the chief defender of Japan's so-called "strong" policy in respect to China. In addition he has been chief political correspondent and editorial contributor to the North-China Daily News. Chinese animosity against Mr. Sokolsky is due largely to the fact that in recent years he has lent himself to various foreign propagandas which have had the effect of neutralizing his previous sympathetic attitude toward the Chinese and their institutions. According to the report which appeared in the Chen Pao, the Kuomintang organ in Nanking, Mr. Sokolsky is alleged to have been the directing genius of various foreign propaganda movements in Shanghai which have had as their object the undermining of the broad objectives of the National Government and the Kuomintang Party from the standpoint of Chinese reconstruction. If the other serious charges which appeared in the semi-official Nanking newspaper are not correct, the proprietors of that paper have laid themselves open to serious action on the basis of criminal libel. A few weeks ago Mr. Sokolsky was elected a member of the executive committee of the American Chamber of Commerce of Shanghai, having been an active member of that organization and its chief adviser on Chinese political and economic affairs for the past three or four years.

The most unfortunate phase of the Chinese Government's action against the North-China Daily News and Mr. Sokolsky, has to do with the indirect effect upon other foreign newspapers and foreign newspapermen in China. While the semi-official explanation of the Government's action which was circulated by Reuters stated that it was not to be interpreted as an indication of any wholesale anti-foreign-press attitude on the part of the Chinese authorities, it is likely to have this effect. Already there are rumors of pending official protests against the writings of other foreign newspapermen and correspondents, which, if carried out would, in all probability react unfavorably upon public opinion abroad in respect to news reports from China. What has happened is that the Chinese authorities are likely to judge all foreign newspapers and newspapermen by the two recent cases which have received official attention, when, as a matter of fact these two cases have been the exception rather than the rule. However, when one realizes what has been taking place in other parts of the world on this question of freedom of the press, it probably is unfair to blame China too severely. There are a number of highly-respectable governments in Europe under the jurisdiction of which freedom of the press is a thing of the past, and while on this subject it is also of interest to recall that the foreign chambers of commerce in Shanghai, and especially the American Chamber, two years ago tried their best to suppress all foreign editorial opinion in Shanghai which did not accord with the views of a small clique of die-hard foreign merchants who were then in control of the Chamber's activities.

The Deportation of Mr. Sokolsky
(Reprinted from The China Critic for April 25, a Chinese-owned and edited magazine)

The decision of the Central Executive Committee of the Kuomintang to deport that eminent journalist, Mr. George E. Sokolsky, and to discipline The North China Daily News for which he writes has been received with the greatest satisfaction in various circles. Ordinarily we do not for a moment advocate the suppression of public opinion on the part of an individual or the press, but when the so-called public opinion becomes malicious propaganda calculated to threaten the foundation of the government, it is then time that an end be put to it. The Daily News has never upheld Chinese nationalism either in principle or in practice though it has chosen at times, for various reasons, to single out particular officials for praise. When the Nationalist troops entered Shanghai, this paper spared no effort to undermine public confidence by broadcasting the rumor of the return of the defeated Sun Chung-fang. Though the new capital has been established for two years, and, the country practically unified, our contemporary is still indulging in the wildest speculation on the future of China. Behind all this stands the figure of Mr. George E. Sokolsky. He is guilty more for what he has written without his signature than for what he has had published under his name. He, together with his superior, Mr. O. M. Green, and with Mr. Rodney Gilbert, forms the well-known triumvirate that would have China partitioned by all the Powers. While their fanatic advocacy of foreign intervention and the Mixed Court will hardly receive the serious attention of the foreign Powers, yet the publication of such malicious propaganda under the protection of extraterritoriality is a challenge to the National Government that cannot be ignored. There are, of course, difficulties in enforcing the decision of the Central Executive Committee. The Daily News is the semi-official organ of the British while Mr. Sokolsky is an American citizen. The Government may refuse The Daily News all mail privileges but we doubt if the American Legation would agree to lose such a valuable asset in Mr. Sokolsky. A policy of non-co-operation may be more effective. Our Jewish friend prides himself upon his intimate contact with the Chinese and capitalizes such contact to the fullest extent. If he were to be ostracised from Chinese society and refused all opportunity to interview the government officials, perhaps his services as a mouthpiece for various interests would diminish in value.

For our affluent journalist himself, however, deportation may be even preferable. He is a great propagandist and believes in wide publicity. If he were to continue writing as before, he would remain but a cog in the wheel of the great machinery set against China. But imagine the notoriety that will accrue to him the minute he is deported. Instantly he will cease to be a paid writer and spring into prominence as a figure of international importance. He will be regarded as a martyr of imperialism, and his name will outshine those of his former superior and associate. Though the famous triumvirate may be thereby considerably weakened, the glory from such sacrifice is most worth while. His articles will be sought after, no longer by the solitary North China Daily News, but by the press all over the world. His lectures will be broadcast over the radio, and his recent masterpiece on the history of the world will be run serially in the newspapers even to the disadvantage of Mr. H. G. Wells. Then proudly will Mr. O. M. Green proclaim to the world: "This is the man I have made."

Some ten years ago Mr. Sokolsky lived in obscurity, sometimes writing and sometimes teaching. He was a faithful follower of Dr. Sun Yat-sen—"follower" in the sense that he pursued the noted revolutionist—and even helped China fight the famous Shantung question. He managed the Bureau of Public Information whence he emerged a full-fledged propagandist. The training and experience he thus gained at the cost of the Chinese he has in later years turned against them. With his association with The Far Eastern Review, that engineering journal that has been devoted almost primarily to Sino-Japanese politics, his fortune has changed. In the course of a few years he has become attached to many an organization. No longer a poor scribe he claims to be one of means. All this from his able pen! With the services he has rendered to the foreign interests and the notoriety that is bound to follow his deportation, Mr. Sokolsky will have a far greater future abroad than in this backward country, and if he were true of his race he would thank the Chinese for this kindly act. For all he seems to be interested in his success, and success he will surely achieve at any price.

The future of The North China Daily News, however, is not so bright as its protege's. With the phenomenal progress in the way of reconstruction China will soon emerge a great united country. Then she will assert her rights as an independent nation and all sources of propaganda against her existing institutions will have to go. With them The North China Daily News unless it changes both its face and its heart. This is precisely the reason why this profit-earning newspaper has stood for every policy to prevent the unification of China and to discredit her good name abroad. As long as extraterritoriality remains in force, it may be difficult to suppress this journal, but the National Government is well within its rights to prohibit the circulation of this propaganda sheet. The Canadian Government during the World War forbade the circulation of the Hearst newspapers because they threatened the cause of the Allies at the most critical hour. China today is in an even more critical stage and may well adopt a similar policy. The decision of the Central Executive Committee, therefore, is based upon the principle of self-preservation—a principle which no civilized state can deny another.

merc（原文不清）随后由索科尔斯基（Sokolsky）接管并维持了一段时间，但最终被出售。索科尔斯基先生随后成为中国政府经济情报局经理，该局由旧北平政府资助，但他最终辞职，转而担任《远东评论》（Far Eastern Review）的编辑，这是一本月刊工程杂志，多年来一直是日本所谓对华“强硬”政策的主要辩护者。此外，他还一直担任《字林西报》（North-China Daily News）的首席政治通讯员和社论撰稿人。中国人对索科尔斯基先生的敌意，很大程度上是由于近年来他迎合各种外国宣传，这抵消了他此前对中国及其机构的同情态度。据南京国民党机关报《晨报》刊登的报道，索科尔斯基被指是上海各种外国宣传运动的幕后策划者，这些运动旨在从中国重建的角度破坏国民政府和国民党的广泛目标。如果这份半官方南京报纸上刊登的其他严重指控不实，则该报业主将因刑事诽谤罪而面临严重的法律行动。几周前，索科尔斯基先生当选为上海美国商会执行委员会成员，他在过去三四年里一直是该组织的活跃成员及其在中国政治和经济事务方面的首席顾问。

中国政府针对《字林西报》和索科尔斯基先生的行动中，最令人遗憾的一面在于其对在华其他外报和外国记者产生的间接影响。虽然路透社散布的政府对此次行动的半官方解释称，不应将其解读为中国当局有任何全面反对外国新闻界态度的迹象，但这很可能产生此类效果。目前已有传言称，当局正准备对其他外国记者和通讯员的报道提出正式抗议，如果付诸实施，很可能会对国外公众舆论关于来自中国的新闻报道产生不利反应。实际情况是，中国当局可能会根据最近两起受到官方关注的案件来评判所有外国报纸和记者，而事实上，这两起案件属于例外而非常态。然而，当人们意识到世界其他地区在新闻自由问题上所发生的情况时，过分严厉地指责中国可能是不公平的。欧洲有一些备受尊敬的政府，在其管辖下，新闻自由已成为过去式；在此话题上，同样值得注意的是，两年前，上海的外国商会，特别是美国商会，曾竭力压制上海所有不符合当时控制商会活动的一小撮顽固外商观点的外国社论意见。

驱逐索科尔斯基先生
（转载自费4月25日出版的《中国评论周报》，一家由中国人拥有和编辑的杂志）

国民党中央执行委员会决定驱逐那位著名记者乔治·E·索科尔斯基（George E. Sokolsky）先生，并惩处他所供稿的《字林西报》，这一决定在各阶层中引起了极大的满意。通常我们绝不主张个人或新闻界压制舆论，但当所谓的舆论变成旨在威胁政府基础的恶意宣传时，就是时候予以终结了。《字林西报》无论在原则上还是实践中，从未维护过中国的民族主义，尽管它有时出于各种原因选择赞扬某些特定官员。当国民革命军进入上海时，该报不遗余力地广播败将孙传芳即将回归的谣言，以此削弱公众信心。虽然新首都已建立两年，国家实际上已统一，但我们的这家同行仍在对中国未来进行最荒谬的猜测。这一切的背后站着乔治·E·索科尔斯基先生。他的罪过更多在于那些未署名的文章，而非以他名义发表的文章。他与他的上级O. M. 格林（O. M. Green）先生以及罗德尼·吉尔伯特（Rodney Gilbert）先生组成了著名的“三巨头”，企图让列强瓜分中国。虽然他们狂热鼓吹外国干预和会审公廨的做法很难得到外国列强的认真对待，但在治外法权的庇护下发布此类恶意宣传，是对国民政府不可忽视的挑战。当然，执行中央执行委员会的决定存在困难。《字林西报》是英国的半官方机关报，而索科尔斯基先生是美国公民。政府可以拒绝给予《字林西报》任何邮件特权，但我们怀疑美国公使馆是否愿意失去索科尔斯基先生这样宝贵的资产。不合作政策可能更为有效。我们的这位犹太朋友以其与中国人的密切接触为荣，并充分利用这种接触。如果他被中国社会排斥，并被拒绝一切采访政府官员的机会，那么他作为各方利益代言人的价值或许会降低。

然而，对于这位富有的记者本人来说，驱逐甚至可能是更可取的选择。他是一位伟大的宣传家，相信广泛的 publicity（公开宣传）。如果他继续像以前那样写作，他将只是反对中国的巨大机器中的一颗齿轮。但想象一下，一旦他被驱逐，他将获得怎样的恶名。他将立即不再是一名受雇作家，而是作为一位具有国际重要性的人物崭露头角。他将被视为帝国主义的烈士，他的名字将盖过他 former superior（前上级）和同事的风头。虽然著名的“三巨头”可能因此大大削弱，但这种牺牲带来的荣耀是最值得的。他的文章将不再仅由孤独的《字林西报》寻求，而是受到全世界新闻界的追捧。他的演讲将通过无线电广播，他最近关于世界历史的杰作将在报纸上连载，甚至让H. G. 威尔斯（H. G. Wells）先生相形见绌。届时，O. M. 格林先生将自豪地向世界宣告：“这是我造就的人。”

大约十年前，索科尔斯基先生默默无闻，时而写作，时而教书。他是孙中山博士的忠实追随者——这里的“追随者”是指他追踪这位著名革命家——甚至帮助中国应对著名的山东问题。他管理公共情报局，从中成长为一名成熟的宣传家。他由此以牺牲中国为代价获得的训练和经验，在后来几年里被用来对付中国人。随着他与《远东评论》的联系，那本几乎主要致力于中日政治的工程杂志，他的命运发生了改变。在几年时间里，他与许多组织建立了联系。他不再是一个贫穷的文人，声称自己富有。这一切都归功于他那支生花妙笔！鉴于他为外国利益提供的服务以及驱逐后必然随之而来的名声，索科尔斯基先生在国外的前途将远大于在这个落后国家的前途，如果他对他的种族忠诚，他应该感谢中国人的这一善意举动。因为他似乎只关心自己的成功，而且他不惜任何代价必将取得成功。

然而，《字林西报》的未来并不像其门徒那样光明。随着重建工作的惊人进展，中国很快就会成为一个统一的伟大国家。那时，她将作为一个独立国家主张自己的权利，所有针对其现有制度的宣传来源都必须消失。《字林西报》也将随之消亡，除非它改头换面、洗心革面。这正是这家盈利报纸支持每一项阻止中国统一、损害中国国际声誉的政策的原因。只要治外法权仍然有效，取缔这家期刊可能很困难，但国民政府完全有权禁止发行这份宣传刊物。世界大战期间，加拿大政府禁止赫斯特（Hearst）报纸的流通，因为它们在关键时刻威胁到协约国的事业。今天的中国处于更加关键的阶段，完全可以采取类似的政策。因此，中央执行委员会的决定是基于自卫原则——这是任何文明国家都不能否认另一国的原则。

THE NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS, WEDNESDAY, MAY 30, 1928

A NEW MOVEMENT TOWARDS RUSSIA
IN NANKING POLITICS

The Breach with Japan and the Old Game of Finding One
Friend Abroad to Make Trouble Among Powers

BUT NO THIRD INTERNATIONALE NEED APPLY

By GEORGE E. SOKOLSKY

The essential factor in Chinese diplomacy since the time of Viceroy Li Hung-chang has been an alliance with one Power in the hope of achieving discord among the Powers interested in China. In May 1896, the secret Li-Lobanoff Treaty between China and Russia provided for a defensive and offensive alliance; it even stated that “no treaty of peace with an adverse party can be concluded by either of them without the consent of the other.” This treaty was aimed at Great Britain and Japan. It was China’s method of destroying every semblance of unity of purpose among the Powers. It must be noted that this Treaty was in operation during the Boxer Rebellion and the Russo-Japanese War. It was in operation when Russia was pursuing a policy of intense imperialism in Manchuria and when Japan was struggling to become a first class Power. It explains more than any other cause the trend of sentiment in Japan which culminated in the Twenty-One Demands, for whereas Japan had not the exact wording of the Li-Lobanoff Treaty until the Washington Conference, all the principal Powers were cognizant of the fact that some agreement of this nature existed.

Some One to Fight Her Battles
The underlying motive of the Li-Lobanoff Agreement, from the Chinese standpoint, was the advantage that might accrue to China from the utilization of one great European Power to protect tangible interests in order, to protect China from the other Powers. In a word, Li Hung-chang conceived the doctrine of China using Russia to fight China’s battles. In return, China conceded to Russia a free hand to follow vast imperialistic programmes in Manchuria and Mongolia which were, after all, only remotely Chinese in historical and political relationships.

With variations on the theme, this policy has continued to this day. The Anfu Club, for instance, sought to utilize the Japanese as Li Hung-chang had the Russians; the Chihli Party under Marshal Wu Pei-fu adhered to the same doctrine in their efforts to develop an association of purposes between themselves and Great Britain. Marshal Feng Yu-hsiang, through the American missionaries, sought special American support but when it failed to materialize, he turned to Russia, which held him dear.

Dr. Sun and the Russians
Dr. Sun Yat-sen pursued the same plan. He first sent agents to Great Britain and the United States and then he turned to Russia and Germany. Perhaps in no country is there such an emphasis on foreign relations as in China. The whole structure of Government seems to be based on foreign relations; even political parties measure their actions by the possibilities of reactions in foreign countries. Dr. Sun, then, when he turned to Russia for an alliance, agreed to permit Soviet Russia, through Comrade Borodin, to reorganize the Kuomintang and the Nationalist Government on a Russian model.

The essential factor to Dr. Sun was not so much what kind of a government China had, as that his revolutionary conceptions should conquer China; that his Nationalist Government should succeed in destroying its opponents and becoming master of the country even to the holding of the capital, Peking. In return, Soviet Russia was given a free hand to use China as a weapon in a war to destroy the British Empire by paralyzing British trade and industry. The Russians succeeded admirably in certain phases of their programme; the Nationalists reached the Yangtze Valley and Shanghai; two foreign concessions, Hankow and Kiukiang, were returned to China inexpensively; labour was organized into C.P. unit and a boycott against British goods was for two years effective.

The Russians, however, failed in one essential: they believed that they were using the Chinese in their quarrel with Great Britain, while, as a matter of fact, the Nationalists were using them in their effort to reach Peking. When it appeared that the Russians were no longer indispensable, they were not only driven from the country, but those who were slow to leave were arrested and made to suffer detention and humiliation.

A Pro-British Orientation
The dismissal of the Russians was not merely the result of Chiang Kai-shek’s engrossing fear of the Chinese C. P. opposition to himself. Nationalist foreign policy hoped to substitute either Great Britain or Japan for Soviet Russia. 《字林西报》，1928年5月30日，星期三

南京政坛中亲俄的新动向

与日本决裂，以及利用一个外国友邦在列强之间制造麻烦的旧把戏

但第三国际恕不接待

乔治·E·索科尔斯基（George E. Sokolsky） 著

自李鸿章总督时代以来，中国外交的核心因素便是与某一强国结盟，以期在关注中国的列强之间制造不和。1896年5月，中俄秘密签订的《李-洛巴诺夫条约》规定了攻守同盟；甚至规定“未经另一方同意，任何一方不得与敌对方缔结和约”。该条约针对的是英国和日本。这是中国用来破坏列强在目的上任何表面团结的手段。必须指出，该条约在义和团运动和日俄战争期间均有效力。当俄国在满洲推行强烈的帝国主义政策，而日本正努力跻身一流强国之列时，该条约也在施行中。这比任何其他原因更能解释日本舆论走向的成因，并最终导致了“二十一条”要求的提出，因为尽管直到华盛顿会议之前日本才得知《李-洛巴诺夫条约》的确切措辞，但所有主要列强都知晓存在某种性质的协定。

找人替她打仗

从中方角度来看，《李-洛巴诺夫协定》的根本动机在于，中国希望通过利用一个欧洲大国来保护其实际利益，从而免受其他列强的侵害。简言之，李鸿章构想出了中国利用俄国为中国打仗的理论。作为回报，中国允许俄国在满洲和蒙古放手推行庞大的帝国主义计划，而这些地区在历史和政治关系上毕竟与中国只有疏远的联系。

尽管主题有所变化，但这一政策一直延续至今。例如，安福俱乐部试图像李鸿章利用俄国那样利用日本人；吴佩孚元帅旗下的直系军阀在其努力发展与英国的共同目标关联时，也奉行同样的理论。冯玉祥元帅通过美国传教士寻求美国的特别支持，但当这一希望落空后，他便转向了珍视他的俄国。

孙中山博士与俄国人

孙中山博士也采取了同样的策略。他先派遣代理人前往英国和美国，随后转向俄国和德国。也许没有任何国家像中国这样强调对外关系。整个政府结构似乎都建立在对外关系之上；甚至各政党也以在国外可能引发的反应来衡量其行动。因此，当孙中山转向俄国寻求结盟时，他同意允许苏维埃俄国通过鲍罗廷同志按照俄国模式改组国民党和国民政府。

对孙中山博士而言，核心因素不在于中国拥有何种类型的政府，而在于他的革命理念应征服中国；他的国民政府应成功摧毁对手并成为国家的主宰，甚至掌控首都北京。作为回报，苏维埃俄国被赋予自由权，将中国作为瓦解大英帝国的战争武器，通过瘫痪英国的贸易和工业来实现这一目标。俄国人在其计划的某些阶段取得了令人瞩目的成功；国民党军队抵达长江流域和上海；汉口和九江两个外国租界以低廉的成本归还中国；劳工被组织成中共单位，且抵制英货的运动在两年内行之有效。

然而，俄国人在一个关键点上失败了：他们以为自己在与英国的争端中利用中国人，而事实上，国民党是在利用他们以实现进军北京的目标。当俄国人显得不再不可或缺时，他们不仅被驱逐出境，那些迟迟不肯离开的人还被逮捕，遭受拘留和羞辱。

Nanking then turned to Japan.
The intrigue to win Japanese support is a fascinating study in diplomacy. Special representatives were sent to Japan who were assumed to be able to handle Japanese political groups. The Ministry of Foreign Affairs went out of its way to satisfy Japanese wishes. Labour and other subversive movements were suppressed to convince the Japanese that Nationalism had turned over a new leaf and that it was prepared to foster Japanese economic interests particularly in the Yangtze Valley. The boycott movement was put down zealously.

The question whether Japan should send troops to Shantung, only a few hundred miles from Nanking and that once Chang Tso-lin and Sun Chuan-fang were eliminated, that Japan should make Chang Tso-lin's position in Peking untenable. There is no indication, beyond the statements of the Nationalist agents in Japan and Mr. Huang Fu, to prove that any responsible Japanese had agreed to this programme. Yet there is the amazing fact that in spite of the Tsinan Incident, the Nationalist Government continues to adhere to it. Nanking is still facing Japan as a possible ally, with arms outstretched in friendship and reconciliation.

The Pro-Russian Party
But the opposition to those in control of the Nanking Government are denouncing Nanking's foreign policy as futile. They say that Nationalism cannot expect special treatment from either Great Britain or Japan, because the interests of both in China are such that they cannot make concessions to Nationalism. For instance, both Great Britain and Japan have outstanding claims which have to be settled; they will not give concessions without considerable negotiations, to say the least, and in the course of these negotiations, Nationalism will have to show up very badly.

They insist that the only hope is in Soviet Russia, which has no interests in China proper, which has no trade and no possessions—which has no genuine outstanding issue with the Nationalists, no Nanking Outrage, no Tsinan Incident. But these people realize that a rapprochement with Soviet Russia would lose the support of Canton and Hankow, that the Kuangsi faction would never agree to it and that the conquered provinces might be alienated by it. Therefore, they propose a governmental alliance rather than a party alliance.

No Third Internationale Wanted
The Borodin association was a party alliance. The Third Internationale supported the Kuomintang. The Russian Communist Party supported the Kuomintang. Comrade Borodin was not an official of the Soviet Russian Government but of the Third Internationale. Now, these neo-Russians advocate an alliance with Soviet Russia through its Ministry of Foreign Affairs without the intervention of the Third Internationale. They suggest that there is at present such an arrangement between Soviet Russia and Turkey; that whereas Turkey forbids Communist activity, either Russian or Turkish, the two countries are in actual alliance. But, ask others, what has Russia to gain if it supports the Nationalists, with both the Russian and Chinese C.P. forbidden in Nationalist territory?

The Chinese C.P.'s Plan
In Moscow, Berlin and Paris, there are large numbers of Nationalist leaders, some of them much more important in party affairs than those who have remained in Nanking. Among them are men who are working for this rapprochement. The Tsinan Incident is being used as the leverage. Can Russia see Japan seize territory in China, they are asking? Furthermore, they are investigating the reported understanding between Japan and Russia arranged by Viscount Goto and Mr. Kuhara. If that understanding does not exist, it is planned that a "Back to Russia," Movement should be developed during the summer. This movement is to be independent of the Chinese Communist Party which, it is said, has other plans, the principal one being an anti-Kuomintang demonstration in Shanghai and the Yangtze Valley on the arrival of the Nationalist armies in Peking.

南京与麦克默里（MacMurray）先生之间的谈判是英国解决方案的附带事项。南京从未指望在美国取得多大成就。他们正在寻求某种秘密安排，而美国的政治体制排除了这种可能性。他们认为参议员博拉（Borah）和一两名国会议员是他们的朋友，但他们意识到自己一事无成。但是，麦克默里协定的直接后果是，使得有关南京事件的讨论在中国人中间变得极不受欢迎，因为人们假定南京永远无法获得比麦克默里先生给予的更好的条件，而更差的条件在中国人的观念中是不可想象的。

接下来是日本

南京随后转向日本。争取日本支持的阴谋活动是外交史上引人入胜的研究课题。特派代表被派往日本，据信他们能够应付日本的政治团体。外交部格外努力地满足日本的愿望。劳工和其他颠覆运动受到镇压，以使日本人相信民族主义已经改头换面，并准备促进日本的经济利益，特别是在长江流域。抵制运动被热心地镇压下去。

关于日本是否应向距离南京仅数百里的山东派兵的问题，以及一旦张作霖和孙传芳被清除，日本应使张作霖在北京的地位站不住脚。除了国民党驻日代理人和黄郛先生的声明外，没有任何迹象表明有任何负责任的日本人同意了这一计划。然而，令人惊讶的事实是，尽管发生了济南惨案，国民政府仍坚持这一计划。南京仍将日本视为可能的盟友，伸出双臂表示友好与和解。

亲俄派

但是，反对南京政府控制者的人士谴责南京的外交政策徒劳无功。他们说，民族主义不能指望从英国或日本那里得到特殊待遇，因为两国在华利益使得它们无法向民族主义做出让步。例如，英国和日本都有未决的索赔要求需要解决；至少可以说，如果不经过大量谈判，它们不会做出让步，而在这些谈判过程中，民族主义的表现将会非常糟糕。

他们坚持认为，唯一的希望在于苏维埃俄国，因为它在中国本土没有利益，没有贸易，也没有财产——它与国民党之间没有真正的未决问题，没有南京事件，也没有济南惨案。但是这些人意识到，与苏维埃俄国修好将失去广州和汉口的支持，桂系永远不会同意，而被征服的省份可能会因此产生异心。因此，他们提议建立政府间的联盟，而不是党派间的联盟。

不需要第三国际

鲍罗廷的关系是一种党派联盟。第三国际支持国民党。俄国共产党支持国民党。鲍罗廷同志不是苏维埃俄国政府的官员，而是第三国际的官员。现在，这些新亲俄派主张通过苏维埃俄国外交部与其结盟，而不让第三国际介入。他们建议，目前苏维埃俄国与土耳其之间就有这样的安排；虽然土耳其禁止无论是俄国还是土耳其的共产主义活动，但两国实际上处于同盟状态。但是，其他人问道，如果俄国人和中国人的共产党都被禁止在国民党领土内活动，俄国支持国民党又能得到什么好处呢？

中共的计划

在莫斯科、柏林和巴黎，有大量国民党领导人，其中一些人在党务方面比留在南京的人重要得多。其中包括致力于这种修好关系的人。济南惨案正被用作杠杆。他们问道，俄国怎能坐视日本在中国夺取领土？此外，他们正在调查据报道由后藤子爵和久原房之介先生安排的日俄谅解。如果这种谅解不存在，则计划在夏季开展一场“回到俄国去”运动。据说，这场运动将独立于中国共产党，后者另有计划，主要计划是在国民党军队抵达北京时，在上海和长江流域举行反国民党示威。
